# MeraLawyer.pk — full content

> MeraLawyer.pk is a legal services platform in Islamabad and Rawalpindi, Pakistan. It matches people with vetted, licensed advocates for family, criminal, property, corporate and overseas Pakistani matters, and provides legal services such as SECP company registration, FBR income tax return filing, NTN and sales tax registration, trademark registration, legal notices, court marriage, khula, succession certificates and property transfer. Fees are quoted upfront. Consultations in Urdu and English.

## Family lawyer in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/hire-a-lawyer/family-lawyer/

A family lawyer represents you in the Family Courts for khula, divorce, child custody, maintenance and dowry recovery. Under the Family Courts Act 1964, these cases are filed in the family court of the area where the wife ordinarily resides. MeraLawyer.pk matches you with a family advocate in Islamabad or Rawalpindi and gives you the full fee before you start.

Cases handled:
- Khula: Dissolution of marriage at the wife's request through the Family Court.
- Divorce (talaq): Talaq notice to the Union Council and the 90-day reconciliation process.
- Child custody: Custody (hizanat) and guardianship petitions under the Guardians and Wards Act 1890.
- Maintenance: Monthly maintenance for wife and children, including arrears.
- Dowry and gifts recovery: Recovery of dowry articles, gold and gifts after separation.
- Restitution of conjugal rights: Petitions to restore the marital home.
- Court marriage: Nikah before a nikah registrar with full documentation.
- Guardianship certificate: Legal guardianship of a minor for property, school or travel.

Q: How much does a family lawyer charge in Islamabad?
A: Fees depend on the type of case, whether it is contested and how many hearings are expected. A simple uncontested matter costs far less than a contested custody case. MeraLawyer.pk gives you the full fee for your case after a free first call.

Q: How long does a family case take?
A: Section 12-A of the Family Courts Act 1964 directs family courts to decide cases within six months of the defendant's first appearance. Contested custody and maintenance cases can take longer in practice.

Q: Can I file a family case if I live abroad?
A: Yes. You can appoint a lawyer through a power of attorney attested at a Pakistani embassy or consulate, and follow the case by WhatsApp and video call.

Q: Which court hears a khula case?
A: The Family Court where the wife ordinarily resides, for example the family courts in Islamabad or Rawalpindi.

## Criminal lawyer in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/hire-a-lawyer/criminal-lawyer/

A criminal lawyer protects you from the moment an FIR is registered: applying for pre-arrest or post-arrest bail, challenging a false FIR, and defending you at trial. Bail is sought under sections 497 and 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before the Sessions Court or the High Court. Tell us your matter is urgent and we prioritise it.

Cases handled:
- Pre-arrest bail: Protective bail before arrest under section 498 CrPC.
- Post-arrest bail: Bail after arrest under section 497 CrPC.
- FIR registration: Help getting an FIR registered, including through a section 22-A petition.
- FIR quashment: Petitions to quash a false or malicious FIR.
- Trial defence: Defence before magistrates and sessions courts.
- Cyber crime: FIA cases under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016.
- Cheque dishonour: Cases under section 489-F of the Pakistan Penal Code.
- Appeals: Criminal appeals and revisions before the High Court.

Q: What is the difference between pre-arrest and post-arrest bail?
A: Pre-arrest bail (section 498 CrPC) protects you from arrest before it happens and is granted only in limited circumstances, such as a malicious case. Post-arrest bail (section 497 CrPC) is sought after you have been arrested.

Q: Can I get bail on the same day?
A: A bail petition can often be filed the same day, but the court decides when to hear it. In urgent matters an interim pre-arrest bail may be granted at the first hearing.

Q: What should I do if a false FIR is registered against me?
A: Do not ignore it. Speak to a criminal lawyer immediately about pre-arrest bail and whether the FIR can be challenged through a quashment petition.

Q: Do you handle FIA cyber crime cases?
A: Yes. Our criminal lawyers handle complaints and defence in FIA cyber crime cases under PECA 2016.

## Property lawyer in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/hire-a-lawyer/property-lawyer/

A property lawyer checks title before you buy, handles transfer and mutation, and takes disputes such as illegal possession, inheritance and rent cases to the civil courts. In Rawalpindi, land records are kept by the Punjab Land Records Authority; in Islamabad, by the ICT revenue office or the CDA, depending on the area. We verify the record before you pay.

Cases handled:
- Property verification: Title, fard and record checks before you buy.
- Transfer and registry: Sale deed, registry and mutation (intiqal).
- Illegal possession: Recovery under the Illegal Dispossession Act 2005.
- Inheritance and partition: Dividing inherited property between legal heirs.
- Rent cases: Eviction and rent recovery before the rent controller.
- Stay orders: Injunctions to stop sale, construction or dispossession.
- Specific performance: Enforcing a sale agreement when the other side backs out.
- Recovery suits: Recovery of money under Order XXXVII CPC.

Q: How do I verify a property before buying in Rawalpindi or Islamabad?
A: Ask for the fard (record of rights) or society allotment and transfer documents, then have a lawyer verify them with the land record office or housing society, check for pending litigation, and confirm the seller's identity.

Q: What can I do if someone illegally occupies my property?
A: You can file a complaint under the Illegal Dispossession Act 2005 and, in parallel, a civil suit for possession. Act quickly and keep proof of ownership.

Q: How is inherited property divided?
A: Shares are fixed by Islamic inheritance law for Muslims. Legal heirs can agree a family settlement, or any heir can file a partition suit in the civil court.

## Corporate and tax lawyer in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/hire-a-lawyer/corporate-lawyer/

A corporate lawyer sets up your business correctly and keeps it compliant: SECP company registration, NTN and sales tax registration with the FBR, annual tax returns, trademark registration with IPO Pakistan, and the contracts your business runs on. MeraLawyer.pk handles the filing for you and quotes a fixed fee upfront.

Cases handled:
- Company registration: Private limited, single-member and public companies with SECP.
- Income tax returns: Annual returns and wealth statements on FBR IRIS.
- NTN registration: National Tax Number for individuals, firms and companies.
- Sales tax registration: FBR for goods; FBR (ICT) or PRA for services.
- Trademark registration: Brand protection with IPO Pakistan.
- Contracts: Shareholder, partnership, employment and service agreements.
- Tax notices: Replies to FBR notices and appeals.
- Banking matters: Recovery suits and defence in banking courts.

Q: Do I need a lawyer to register a company?
A: It is not legally required, but a lawyer or corporate consultant ensures your memorandum and articles of association, shareholding and filings are correct, which prevents problems with banks, FBR and investors later.

Q: Is a sole proprietorship or a private limited company better?
A: A sole proprietorship is cheaper and faster to set up but you are personally liable for its debts. A private limited company separates your personal assets from the business and is preferred by banks, investors and large clients.

Q: When is the income tax return due in Pakistan?
A: For individuals and AOPs the due date is usually 30 September each year for the previous tax year, unless the FBR announces an extension.

## Lawyer for overseas Pakistanis
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/hire-a-lawyer/overseas-pakistani-lawyer/

Overseas Pakistanis can run legal matters in Islamabad and Rawalpindi without flying home. You appoint a lawyer through a power of attorney attested at a Pakistani embassy or consulate, then follow your case by WhatsApp and video call. We handle property recovery, family cases, succession, tax filing and document attestation.

Cases handled:
- Power of attorney: Drafting and guidance on embassy attestation.
- Property recovery: Removing illegal occupants from your property.
- Property management: Rent collection and tenant issues.
- Family cases from abroad: Khula, divorce and custody cases.
- Succession: Succession certificates and inheritance.
- Document attestation: MOFA, HEC, IBCC and embassy attestation.
- Overseas tax return: Non-resident tax filing with FBR.
- Police character certificate: For visa and employment abroad.

Q: Can I fight a property case in Pakistan while living abroad?
A: Yes. You authorise a lawyer or a trusted relative through a power of attorney attested at the Pakistani embassy or consulate, and your lawyer appears in court for you.

Q: How do I attest a power of attorney abroad?
A: Sign it before the consular officer at the Pakistani embassy or consulate, or through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' online e-attestation and consular facilities where available. In Pakistan it may then need to be registered with the sub-registrar for property use.

Q: How will I know what is happening in my case?
A: Your lawyer sends an update after every hearing by WhatsApp, along with copies of orders when they are issued.

## Company registration in Pakistan with SECP
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/company-registration/

Company registration in Pakistan is done online with the Securities and Exchange Commission of Pakistan (SECP). You reserve a company name, submit the memorandum and articles of association with director and shareholder details, pay the SECP fee, and receive a certificate of incorporation. We prepare and file everything for you.

Process:
1. Choose the structure: We advise on the company type, shareholding and number of directors.
2. Reserve the name: We search and reserve an available name with SECP.
3. Prepare documents: We draft the MOA and AOA and collect director details.
4. File with SECP: We submit the incorporation application and pay the fee.
5. Receive certificate: SECP issues your certificate of incorporation.
6. Register for tax: We register the company's NTN with the FBR.

Documents required:
- CNIC copies of all directors and shareholders (passport for foreigners)
- Proposed company names (three options)
- Registered office address and proof
- Nature of business
- Email and mobile number of each director
- Shareholding percentages

Laws: Companies Act 2017; Companies (Incorporation) Regulations 2017

Q: How long does company registration take in Pakistan?
A: When documents are complete, SECP often processes online incorporation within a few working days. Name objections or missing documents add time.

Q: What is the minimum number of directors?
A: A single-member company needs one director and one nominee. A private limited company needs at least two members and two directors.

Q: Can a foreigner register a company in Pakistan?
A: Yes. Foreign nationals can be shareholders and directors, subject to security clearance by the Ministry of Interior, which SECP arranges.

Q: Is there a minimum paid-up capital?
A: There is no general minimum for private companies, although some regulated sectors set their own requirements.

## Income tax return filing in Pakistan
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/income-tax-return/

An income tax return is filed online on the FBR's IRIS portal, usually by 30 September for the previous tax year. Individuals also file a wealth statement listing assets and liabilities. Filing puts you on the Active Taxpayers List, which lowers withholding tax on property, vehicles and banking. We prepare and file your return for you.

Process:
1. Share your details: Send salary certificates, bank statements and asset details.
2. We calculate tax: We work out your tax liability and adjustable taxes.
3. You review: You approve the return and wealth statement before filing.
4. We file on IRIS: We submit the return and send you the acknowledgement.

Documents required:
- CNIC
- IRIS login or registered mobile and email
- Salary certificate or business income records
- Bank account statements and withholding tax certificates
- Property, vehicle and investment details
- Previous year's return, if filed

Laws: Income Tax Ordinance 2001; Income Tax Rules 2002

Q: What is the deadline for filing income tax returns?
A: The due date for individuals is normally 30 September for the tax year ending 30 June. The FBR sometimes extends it, so check the current year's announcement.

Q: What happens if I file late?
A: You can still file, but late filing can attract penalties and you may need to pay a surcharge to get onto the Active Taxpayers List for that year.

Q: Do overseas Pakistanis need to file returns?
A: Non-residents with Pakistan-source income, or who want lower withholding tax on property deals, often benefit from filing.

Q: What is a wealth statement?
A: A statement of your assets and liabilities at the end of the tax year, required with the return for most individuals.

## NTN registration in Pakistan
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/ntn-registration/

An NTN (National Tax Number) is your registration with the Federal Board of Revenue. For individuals, the NTN is the same as the CNIC number once registered on the FBR's IRIS portal. Businesses, AOPs and companies receive their own NTN. Registration needs a CNIC, a mobile number registered in your own name, an email and an address.

Process:
1. Send your details: CNIC, mobile, email, address and business information.
2. We register on IRIS: We complete the registration and verification codes.
3. Business details: We add business name, address and activity where needed.
4. Get your certificate: You receive your NTN certificate.

Documents required:
- CNIC
- Mobile number registered in your name
- Email address
- Residential and business address
- For AOPs: partnership deed and partners' CNICs
- For companies: certificate of incorporation

Laws: Income Tax Ordinance 2001, section 181

Q: Is my CNIC number my NTN?
A: For individuals registered on IRIS, yes: the CNIC number serves as the NTN.

Q: How long does NTN registration take?
A: Individual registration is often completed the same day once verification codes are received. Business and company NTNs can take longer if documents are requested.

Q: Do freelancers need an NTN?
A: Freelancers receiving foreign remittances benefit from registering and filing returns, and may qualify for reduced tax treatment on IT export income.

## Sales tax registration in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/sales-tax-registration/

Sales tax on goods is registered with the FBR under the Sales Tax Act 1990. Sales tax on services depends on where you provide them: in Islamabad it falls under the Islamabad Capital Territory (Tax on Services) Ordinance 2001, collected by the FBR; in Rawalpindi it is registered with the Punjab Revenue Authority (PRA). We register you and file monthly returns.

Process:
1. Assess your business: We confirm whether you deal in goods, services or both, and where.
2. Collect documents: We gather business, bank and premises details.
3. Register: We file with the FBR or PRA, including any biometric verification step.
4. Monthly filing: We file your monthly returns so you stay compliant.

Documents required:
- NTN and CNIC of owner or directors
- Business premises proof (rent agreement or ownership)
- Business bank account certificate
- Utility bill of business premises
- Photos and GPS location of premises, if required
- Electricity meter details for manufacturers

Laws: Sales Tax Act 1990; Islamabad Capital Territory (Tax on Services) Ordinance 2001; Punjab Sales Tax on Services Act 2012

Q: Do I register with FBR or PRA?
A: For goods, the FBR. For services, it depends on where the service is provided: Islamabad services fall under ICT (administered by FBR), Punjab services under the PRA.

Q: Do I have to file a return if I had no sales?
A: Yes. Registered persons generally must file a monthly return even when it is a nil return.

Q: What happens if I do not register?
A: Unregistered businesses that are required to register can face penalties, higher withholding and loss of business with clients who need sales tax invoices.

## Trademark registration in Pakistan
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/trademark-registration/

A trademark is registered with the Intellectual Property Organization of Pakistan (IPO Pakistan) under the Trade Marks Ordinance 2001. The process is: search, file an application in the right class, respond to examination, publication in the Trade Marks Journal for opposition, then registration. Registration lasts ten years and can be renewed.

Process:
1. Search: We check the register for similar marks.
2. File: We file your application in the right class.
3. Examination: We respond to any objections from the registrar.
4. Publication: Your mark is published for opposition.
5. Registration: You receive the registration certificate.

Documents required:
- Brand name and logo (if any)
- Applicant CNIC, or company incorporation certificate
- Description of goods or services
- Date of first use, if already in use
- Authorisation letter

Laws: Trade Marks Ordinance 2001; Trade Marks Rules 2004

Q: How long is a trademark valid in Pakistan?
A: Ten years from the filing date, renewable for further ten-year periods.

Q: Can I use TM before registration?
A: Yes, TM can be used to claim a mark. The registered symbol should only be used once the mark is registered.

Q: How long does trademark registration take?
A: It usually takes many months because of examination and the opposition period. You get a filing number immediately, which establishes your priority date.

## Legal notice drafted by an advocate
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/legal-notice/

A legal notice is a formal letter from your advocate telling the other side what they owe you or must stop doing, and what legal action follows if they do not comply. It is often the fastest way to settle money recovery, rent, employment and contract disputes without going to court. Notices to government bodies are required before suing under section 80 CPC.

Process:
1. Tell us the facts: Share what happened and any documents.
2. We draft: Your advocate drafts the notice and you approve it.
3. We send: It is sent with proof of delivery.
4. Follow up: We advise on the reply or next legal step.

Documents required:
- Your CNIC
- Name and address of the other party
- Agreements, cheques, receipts, messages or emails
- Amount owed or action demanded

Laws: Code of Civil Procedure 1908, section 80 (notices to government); Defamation Ordinance 2002; Contract Act 1872

Q: Is a legal notice compulsory before filing a case?
A: Not always. It is required before suing the government (section 80 CPC) and before a defamation suit, and it is strongly advisable in most money and contract disputes.

Q: What if the other side ignores the notice?
A: You can proceed with a civil suit, recovery suit or other action. The notice becomes evidence that you tried to settle.

Q: How should I reply to a legal notice I received?
A: Do not ignore it. Have a lawyer reply within the time given, denying wrong claims, so the record reflects your position.

## Agreement and contract drafting
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/agreements/

A well-drafted agreement prevents most disputes. In Pakistan, agreements such as property sale and rent agreements are executed on stamp paper of the correct value, signed before witnesses, and in some cases registered with the sub-registrar. Our lawyers draft and review agreements so your money and rights are protected.

Process:
1. Tell us the deal: Parties, amounts, dates and conditions.
2. Draft: We draft the agreement in clear language.
3. Revise: You and the other party review changes.
4. Execute: We guide signing, witnesses, stamp paper and registration.

Documents required:
- CNIC copies of all parties
- Property documents, for property agreements
- Agreed terms (price, rent, duration, payment schedule)
- Two witnesses with CNICs

Laws: Contract Act 1872; Stamp Act 1899; Registration Act 1908; Partnership Act 1932

Q: Does a rent agreement need to be registered?
A: Leases for more than one year must be registered under the Registration Act 1908. Shorter agreements are commonly made on stamp paper, and some areas also require tenant registration with police.

Q: Is an agreement on plain paper valid?
A: It can be valid as a contract, but insufficient stamp duty can make it inadmissible as evidence until the duty and penalty are paid.

Q: Can you review an agreement before I sign?
A: Yes. We review it and point out risky clauses before you sign.

## Court marriage in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/court-marriage/

Court marriage in Pakistan is a nikah performed with the free consent of both adults, usually at a lawyer's office, with a nikah registrar and two witnesses. The nikahnama is registered with the Union Council under the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961, after which a NADRA computerised marriage certificate can be issued. Both parties must be adults.

Process:
1. Consultation: We confirm eligibility and documents.
2. Affidavits: Both parties sign affidavits of free consent.
3. Nikah: The nikah is performed with witnesses.
4. Registration: We register the nikahnama and arrange the NADRA certificate.

Documents required:
- Original CNICs of bride and groom
- Passport-size photographs
- CNICs of two adult male witnesses
- Divorce or death certificate, if previously married
- Written permission of the arbitration council, if the man has an existing wife

Laws: Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961; Child Marriage Restraint Act 1929 (and ICT Child Marriage Restraint Act 2025)

Q: Can court marriage be done on the same day?
A: The nikah and affidavits can usually be completed the same day. Union Council registration and the NADRA certificate follow afterwards.

Q: Is court marriage legal without parents' consent?
A: Under Pakistani law an adult Muslim woman can marry with her own free consent. The nikah must still be properly registered.

Q: What is the minimum age for marriage?
A: Both parties must be adults. In Islamabad the minimum age for both is 18 under recent federal legislation, and you should confirm the current rule for the province where the nikah is registered.

## Khula in Pakistan: procedure and documents
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/khula/

Khula is a divorce initiated by the wife through the Family Court. She files a suit for dissolution of marriage, the court attempts reconciliation, and if it fails the court dissolves the marriage, usually on the wife returning the dower (haq mehr) received. The decree is then sent to the Union Council, which issues an effective divorce certificate after the 90-day period.

Process:
1. Consultation: We review your nikahnama and situation.
2. File the suit: We file in the family court where you reside.
3. Summons: The court summons the husband.
4. Reconciliation: The court holds pre-trial reconciliation.
5. Decree: If reconciliation fails, the court passes a decree of khula.
6. Union Council: The decree goes to the Union Council for the divorce certificate.

Documents required:
- Nikahnama
- Your CNIC and the husband's CNIC copy or details
- Husband's current address
- Children's B-forms, if claiming custody or maintenance
- Proof of dowry articles, if claiming them

Laws: Family Courts Act 1964; Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act 1939; Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961

Q: How long does khula take in Pakistan?
A: The court hearing stage can be quick if the husband does not contest. After the decree, the Union Council process takes about 90 days before the divorce becomes effective.

Q: Do I have to return the haq mehr?
A: The court may order the wife to return the dower she received, or part of it. Deferred dower that was never paid is usually not returned.

Q: Can I file khula from abroad?
A: Yes, through a lawyer authorised by an attested power of attorney. The court may need your statement, which can sometimes be arranged by video link.

Q: Can I claim maintenance and custody with khula?
A: Yes. Claims for maintenance, dowry articles and custody can be combined in the same family suit.

## Succession certificate in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/succession-certificate/

A succession certificate lets legal heirs claim a deceased person's bank accounts, shares and other movable assets. Where all heirs agree, it can be obtained from a NADRA Succession Facilitation Unit under the Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Act 2020 (Islamabad) or the Punjab Act 2021 (Rawalpindi). If heirs disagree, a petition is filed in the civil court under the Succession Act 1925.

Process:
1. Check eligibility: We confirm heirs and which route applies.
2. Collect documents: Death certificate, FRC and asset details.
3. Apply: We apply at NADRA or file a petition in court.
4. Objections period: Notice is published so objections can be raised.
5. Certificate issued: The certificate is issued and assets released.

Documents required:
- Death certificate (NADRA computerised)
- Family registration certificate (FRC)
- CNICs of all legal heirs
- Deceased's CNIC
- Details of bank accounts and assets
- Affidavits of heirs

Laws: Succession Act 1925; Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Act 2020 (ICT); Punjab Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Act 2021

Q: Which is faster, NADRA or court?
A: The NADRA route is usually faster when all legal heirs agree. If there is any dispute among heirs, the matter goes to the civil court.

Q: Can a woman heir apply?
A: Yes. Every legal heir, male or female, is entitled to their share and can participate in the application.

Q: Do I need a succession certificate for property?
A: Immovable property is usually transferred through inheritance mutation (intiqal) with the land record office. A letter of administration may be needed in some cases.

## Property verification before you buy
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/property-verification/

Property verification means confirming that the seller truly owns the property, that it is free from disputes, mortgages and stay orders, and that the documents match the official record. In Rawalpindi, this means checking the fard with the Punjab Land Records Authority; in Islamabad, the ICT revenue or CDA record; and for housing societies, the society's own transfer record.

Process:
1. Send the documents: Share whatever the seller has given you.
2. Record check: We verify with the relevant land or society office.
3. Litigation search: We check for pending cases and stay orders.
4. Report: You get a written report with risks and next steps.

Documents required:
- Copy of the seller's CNIC
- Fard, registry, allotment or transfer letter
- Society NOC or file number
- Map or plot number
- Any agreement already signed

Laws: Registration Act 1908; Transfer of Property Act 1882; Punjab Land Revenue Act 1967

Q: Why verify a property if the seller has the original documents?
A: Fraud through forged or duplicate documents, sales by someone without authority, and properties under a stay order are common. Only the official record confirms the true position.

Q: Should I pay an advance before verification?
A: Avoid paying a large advance until verification is complete. If you must, use a written agreement with clear refund terms.

Q: Can you verify a property in a housing society?
A: Yes. We verify with the society's record and check the society's own approval status.

## Property transfer, registry and mutation
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/property-transfer/

Property in Pakistan is transferred by a registered sale deed (registry) with the sub-registrar, followed by mutation (intiqal) in the land record so the new owner appears in the fard. Transfers within families can be done by gift deed (hiba), and inherited property by inheritance mutation. Taxes and stamp duty are paid before registration.

Process:
1. Verify: We verify the property first.
2. Draft: We draft the sale deed or gift deed.
3. Pay taxes: Stamp duty, CVT and withholding taxes are paid.
4. Register: The deed is registered with the sub-registrar.
5. Mutation: The record is updated in the new owner's name.

Documents required:
- CNICs of buyer, seller and two witnesses
- Ownership documents and fard
- NOC from society or CDA, where applicable
- Tax payment challans
- Photographs of the parties

Laws: Registration Act 1908; Transfer of Property Act 1882; Stamp Act 1899; Income Tax Ordinance 2001 (sections 236C and 236K)

Q: What is the difference between registry and mutation?
A: Registry is the registration of the sale deed with the sub-registrar. Mutation (intiqal) updates the land record so the new owner appears in the fard. Both are needed.

Q: Is a gift deed taxed?
A: Gifts between close family members are treated differently from sales, but stamp duty and registration fees still apply. We calculate the exact cost for your case.

Q: Do active taxpayers pay less tax on property?
A: Yes. Withholding tax on buying and selling property is lower for people on the FBR's Active Taxpayers List.

## Power of attorney in Pakistan
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/power-of-attorney/

A power of attorney lets someone act for you. A general power of attorney covers broad matters; a special power of attorney is limited to one task, such as selling a specific property. Overseas Pakistanis sign it before the Pakistani embassy or consulate; for property dealings it is then registered with the sub-registrar in Pakistan.

Process:
1. Define the powers: We agree exactly what the attorney may do.
2. Draft: We draft the POA for you to sign.
3. Attest: You sign before the embassy, or a notary in Pakistan.
4. Register: We register it where required.

Documents required:
- CNIC or NICOP of the principal
- CNIC of the attorney
- Property details, for property-related POA
- Two witnesses
- Passport-size photographs

Laws: Powers of Attorney Act 1882; Registration Act 1908

Q: Can I sell property through a power of attorney?
A: Yes, if the POA specifically authorises it and is registered. Buyers and registrars usually require a registered special POA for property sales.

Q: How do I cancel a power of attorney?
A: Execute a revocation deed, register it where the POA was registered, and notify the attorney and relevant offices.

Q: Is a POA from abroad valid in Pakistan?
A: Yes, when it is attested by the Pakistani embassy or consulate and, for property, registered in Pakistan.

## Bail application in Islamabad and Rawalpindi
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/legal-services/bail-application/

Bail is applied for under section 497 (post-arrest) or section 498 (pre-arrest) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, usually first before the Sessions Court and then, if refused, before the Islamabad High Court or the Lahore High Court Rawalpindi Bench. The lawyer files the petition with the FIR copy and argues why the accused should be released or protected from arrest.

Process:
1. Call us: Tell us it is urgent and share the FIR number and police station.
2. Review: Your lawyer reviews the FIR and grounds.
3. File: The bail petition is filed in the right court.
4. Hearing: Your lawyer argues the bail.
5. Release: Surety bonds are submitted for release.

Documents required:
- Copy of the FIR
- CNIC of the accused
- Surety's CNIC and property or income documents
- Any documents supporting innocence

Laws: Code of Criminal Procedure 1898, sections 496 to 498; Pakistan Penal Code 1860

Q: Which court do I apply to for bail?
A: Usually the Sessions Court first. If bail is refused, you can apply to the High Court.

Q: Is bail available in non-bailable offences?
A: Yes, bail can be granted in non-bailable offences at the court's discretion. It is harder in offences carrying severe punishment.

Q: What is a surety?
A: A person who guarantees the accused will attend court, usually by submitting a bond backed by property or income documents.

## Hire a lawyer in Islamabad
URL: https://meralawyer.pk/lawyer-in-islamabad/

MeraLawyer.pk connects you with vetted advocates who practise in Islamabad's courts: the Islamabad High Court, the District and Sessions Courts (East and West), the family courts and the banking courts. ## General questions

Q: How much does it cost to hire a lawyer in Pakistan?
A: Lawyers' fees depend on the type of case, the court, and how many hearings are expected. MeraLawyer.pk gives you the full fee for your case after a free first call, before you commit to anything.

Q: How does MeraLawyer.pk work?
A: You tell us about your matter by phone, WhatsApp or the form. A case manager understands it and matches you with a vetted advocate in Islamabad or Rawalpindi who handles that type of case. You agree the fee, and the lawyer takes over.

Q: Are your lawyers licensed?
A: Yes. Every lawyer we work with is an advocate enrolled with the relevant bar council, and we check credentials before they join.

Q: Which courts do your lawyers appear in?
A: The Islamabad High Court, the Lahore High Court Rawalpindi Bench, the district and sessions courts of Islamabad and Rawalpindi, family courts, banking courts and tribunals.

Q: Can overseas Pakistanis hire a lawyer through you?
A: Yes. You can brief a lawyer by WhatsApp or video call and authorise them through a power of attorney attested at a Pakistani embassy or consulate.

Q: Is my information confidential?
A: Yes. What you share is used only to match you with a lawyer and is not shared with anyone else.

Q: Do you offer consultations in Urdu?
A: Yes. Consultations are available in Urdu and English.
